subject: dead whale on beach
title: What If You Blew Up a Dead Whale With Dynamite? Oregon Tried in 1970

scenes.text: What if you removed a dead whale with half a ton of dynamite? Oregon tried.
November 1970. A 45-foot, eight-ton sperm whale washes up at Florence, Oregon, rotting. Nobody wants to cut it up.
The state highway division decides to blast it, hoping the pieces will be small enough for gulls and crabs.
November 12. About half a ton of dynamite goes in. A crowd watches from what they think is a safe distance. Boom.
Blubber flies hundreds of feet up and rains down on the beach, the crowd and the parked cars. One slab crushes a car.
And most of the whale was still there. Workers hauled it away. Today Florence has an Exploding Whale Memorial Park.

description:
What if you blew up a dead whale? In November 1970 a 45-foot, eight-ton sperm whale washed up at Florence, Oregon, and the state highway division packed it with about half a ton of dynamite, hoping scavengers would finish the small pieces.
On 12 November the blast sent blubber hundreds of feet into the air and onto the crowd and parked cars, crushing one car, while most of the carcass stayed on the beach to be cleared by hand. Florence now has an Exploding Whale Memorial Park.
